grammar.title: Advanced Idioms & Fixed Expressions
grammar.content:
B2 learners are expected to use idiomatic expressions naturally in conversation. These fixed phrases cannot be translated literally — they must be learned as whole units.

**Opinion & Agreement:**
- 'No estoy de acuerdo contigo' — I disagree with you
- 'Pongamos que... (hipotéticamente)' — Let's say... (hypothetically)
- 'En mi opinión / En mi concepto' — In my opinion
- 'Desde mi punto de vista' — From my point of view

**Cause & Consequence:**
- 'Por un lado... por otro lado...' — On one hand... on the other hand...
- 'A fin de cuentas' — After all / At the end of the day
- 'En última instancia' — Ultimately / In the last instance
- 'Por si fuera poco' — To make matters worse / On top of that

**Social & Professional:**
- 'Llevarse bien/mal con alguien' — To get along well/poorly with someone
- 'Echar de menos' — To miss someone (different from 'extrañar' — more emotional)
- 'Poner las cartas sobre la mesa' — To lay cards on the table (be direct)
- 'Tomar las riendas' — To take the reins (take charge)

**Common B2 Idioms:**
- 'Salirse con la suya' — To get one's way
- 'Hacer la vista gorda' — To turn a blind eye
- 'Ir de capa caída' — To be doing badly / to be in decline
- 'Estar en las nubes' — To be absent-minded / daydreaming
- 'Costar un ojo de la cara' — To cost an arm and a leg

rows: Poner las cartas sobre la mesa
To put the cards on the table
To be direct / reveal your position
To turn a blind eye / ignore wrong
To go with the cape fallen
To be in decline / doing badly
Costar un ojo de la cara
To cost an eye of the face
To make matters worse / on top of that

examples: Voy a poner las cartas sobre la mesa: no puedo seguir así. (I'm going to lay my cards on the table: I can't keep going like this.)
Me echas mucho de menos cuando no estás. (You really miss someone when they're not around.)
Siempre se sale con la suya porque su padre es el jefe. (He always gets his way because his father is the boss.)
El gobierno está haciendo la vista gorda con la corrupción. (The government is turning a blind eye to corruption.)
La empresa va de capa caída desde la crisis. (The company has been in decline since the crisis.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian has equivalent idioms for most of these: 'a pune cărțile pe masă' = poner las cartas sobre la mesa (identical!), 'a ieși cu a ta' = salirse con la suya, 'a face ochiul orb' = hacer la vista gorda. The Romanian 'a da cu părerea' is similar to 'poner las cartas sobre la mesa' in informal contexts.

exercises.question: What does 'poner las cartas sobre la mesa' mean?
options: To be direct / reveal your position
To throw cards on the table
exercises.explanation: 'Poner las cartas sobre la mesa' means 'to lay cards on the table' — to be direct and honest about your position.

exercises.question: What does 'echar de menos' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Echar de menos' = 'to miss someone emotionally.' It's different from 'extrañar' — it expresses a deeper emotional connection.

exercises.question: What does 'salirse con la suya' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Salirse con la suya' = 'to get one's way' — to succeed in doing what one wants.

exercises.question: What does 'ir de capa caída' mean?
options: To be in decline / doing badly
exercises.explanation: 'Ir de capa caída' = 'to be in decline / doing badly.' The imagery is of someone walking with a drooping cape.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Voy a ____ (lay my cards) sobre la mesa.' (I'm going to lay my cards on the table.)
exercises.explanation: 'Voy a poner las cartas sobre la mesa' = I'm going to lay my cards on the table (be direct).

exercises.question: What does 'costar un ojo de la cara' mean?
options: To cost an arm and a leg (very expensive)
exercises.explanation: 'Costar un ojo de la cara' = 'to cost an arm and a leg' — to be very expensive.
